newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran says unhappy with drop in oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Iran says unhappy with drop in oil prices.

text.p: Iran on Sunday urged fellow OPEC members to abide by their quotas to reverse the fall in oil prices.

"Oil prices have dropped by $3.5 (a barrel) since the last OPEC meeting (in November) and we are not satisfied with this situation and OPEC members and others should be aware of that," Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh told a news conference in Kuwait.

"They must monitor this situation. If this situation towards a drop in prices continues the circumstances would become more difficult for us. All must abide and help boost the market," said the minister, whose country is the world's second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.

He said he discussed the issue with his Kuwaiti counterpart and "our views were identical and the two states stress that OPEC members should abide by their quotas and if they do we can stop this drop."
World oil prices fell to six-month lows on Friday to just under $20 -- dropping by 20 percent over the last six weeks.

When asked if the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) should cut the production ceiling at the next ministerial meeting in June, Aghazadeh said: "As for June it is too early to speak about this issue."
On Saturday, British Petroleum Plc's Chief Executive John Browne told Reuters in Kuwait world oil prices could average between $16-$18 a barrel over the next few years.
But Aghazadeh refused to answer any questions on his views on the direction of the world market as cold weather in the northern hemisphere eases and stocks grow.

Other Iranian sources told Reuters that Tehran still sees demand on stocks that could stabilise the market at current levels or drop slightly before picking up again by the end of the third quarter of 1997.
OPEC put its January output at 25.38 million barrels per day (bpd) while a Reuters survey estimated output at 26.64 million bpd. The 11-member cartel has an official ceiling of 25.033 million bpd.
